NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas.

This OPENS the procurement module (third business module). You build the module skeleton + vendor master; the P2P chain (requisition→RFQ→PO→GR→3-way match) comes in 6.2–6.4.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md Procurement section (vendor master = FULL; "approved items" = partial info-record, no time-dependent pricing in v1); docs/architecture.md D-029 (OPAQUE cross-module ids — finance AP already stores vendor as an opaque partner_id with denormalized partner_name and NO FK; procurement now OWNS the vendor entity, and finance/inventory reference it by opaque id; procurement may import finance/queries + inventory/queries downward), D-012/D-013/D-014 (numbering/idempotency/pagination), D-015 (money/qty types), D-022/D-025 (migrations/tests), D-007 (tenancy). Then read the EXACT patterns to mirror — do NOT reinvent:
- backend/app/modules/inventory/ as the freshest full module example: __init__.py, constants.py, models/ (package), schemas.py, service/ (package), queries.py, router.py, and how it's mounted in backend/app/main.py
- backend/app/modules/finance/queries.py (the queries-interface shape) + backend/app/modules/finance/models/payables.py (how AP's VendorBill stores partner_id opaque + partner_name — your vendor's id is exactly that partner_id)
- backend/app/modules/inventory/queries.py (item_exists / get_item — you'll validate approved-item links against this)
- backend/app/core/{models.py (mixins, tenant_fk, tenant_unique, UuidPKMixin, money/qty types), rbac.py (register_permissions), conditional.py (ETag for reference lists), pagination.py, deps.py}
- backend/tests/modules/inventory/factories.py + conftest.py (factory/fixture pattern; the principal + permission wiring)
Latest migration = 0023.

TASK — PLAN 6.1: vendor master + module skeleton. Build:

1. `backend/app/modules/procurement/__init__.py`, `constants.py`:
   - Enums: PaymentTermsBasis or just a PaymentTerm reference? Vendors carry payment terms that drive bill due dates. Model payment terms as a small enum/value set OR a `net_days` integer on the vendor (simplest, matches how AP computes due dates). DECIDE: store `payment_terms_days` (int, e.g. 30 = NET30) on the vendor directly — document; richer term schedules (2/10 net 30) are a later. Add a VendorStatus (ACTIVE | BLOCKED | INACTIVE) — BLOCKED vendors can't receive new POs (used by 6.2 later).
   - Permissions: procurement.vendor.read, procurement.vendor.manage.
   - Vendor codes: user-supplied unique per tenant (mirror inventory item_code / finance account code) — no auto-sequence. Document.
2. `backend/app/modules/procurement/models.py` (split into models/ package only if >400 lines — start single):
   - `Vendor` (`proc_vendors`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin; vendor_code (UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_code)), name, status (VendorStatus), default_currency_code (str(3)), payment_terms_days (int, default 30, CHECK >= 0), tax_reference (str nullable), email/phone/address fields (keep modest — name + a couple contact fields), notes (str nullable). The vendor's id IS the partner_id finance AP stores (D-029). tenant_unique() + tenant_fk to adm_tenants.
   - `VendorApprovedItem` (`proc_vendor_approved_items`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin; vendor_id (composite tenant_fk to proc_vendors), item_id (OPAQUE inventory item id — validate via inventory/queries, NO cross-module FK per D-029; store as Uuid column, NOT a tenant_fk to inv_items), vendor_item_code (str nullable — the vendor's own SKU), is_active. UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_id, item_id). This is the v1 "approved items" info-record-lite (no price/lead-time per parity — those are the documented later).
3. `backend/app/modules/procurement/schemas.py`: Pydantic v2 Create/Update/Read/Filter for Vendor + VendorApprovedItem (money/qty as strings if any; here mostly scalars). 
4. `backend/app/modules/procurement/service.py` (split into service/ package if >400): vendor CRUD (validate vendor_code unique via DB + friendly error; default_currency_code exists in finance — call finance/queries.currency_exists or similar, ADD it to finance/queries if absent following its shape; payment_terms_days >= 0; status transitions: ACTIVE↔BLOCKED↔INACTIVE allowed, document any restriction); approved-item management (add/remove/list; validate the item_id exists in inventory via inventory/queries.item_exists; a vendor can't approve the same item twice → rely on UNIQUE + friendly error). 
5. `backend/app/modules/procurement/queries.py`: the read interface 6.2–6.4 + finance reporting will use — `get_vendor(session, tenant_id, vendor_id)`, `vendor_exists`, `get_vendor_for_partner(partner_id)` (= get_vendor — AP reporting resolves a bill's partner_id to a vendor name/terms), `is_item_approved_for_vendor(vendor_id, item_id)`, `vendor_payment_terms_days(vendor_id)`, `vendor_default_currency(vendor_id)`. Keep it the ONLY file other modules import.
6. `backend/app/modules/procurement/router.py`: REST under /api/v1/procurement: vendors (CRUD, list paginated + filter by status + ETag since reference data), vendor approved-items (nested: GET/POST /vendors/{id}/approved-items, DELETE /vendors/{id}/approved-items/{itemId}). Permission-guard all; mount in main.py create_app. Thin routers. PERFORMANCE §6 (paginated, ≤3 budgets, indexes incl. (tenant_id, status) for the vendor list filter).
7. NO events.py/handlers.py yet (vendor master drives no cross-module effects; the P2P documents in 6.2+ will). Don't create empty files.
8. Migration `0024_procurement_vendors.py` (down_revision 0023): proc_vendors + proc_vendor_approved_items + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
9. `docs/modules/procurement.md`: NEW module guide (vendor master, the partner_id/opaque-id relationship with finance AP, approved-items-as-info-record-lite, payment terms → due dates, the queries interface, what's deferred per parity). 
10. Tests `backend/tests/modules/procurement/` (mirror inventory test layout): conftest.py + factories.py (build_vendor / build_approved_item; a procurement principal with the procurement perms; reuse the shared tenant/auth + finance currency + inventory item fixtures so approved-item validation has a real item to point at), test_vendors.py (CRUD + validation: code unique, currency exists in finance, payment terms >= 0, status transitions), test_approved_items.py (add/remove/list, item-exists validation against inventory, no duplicate), test_vendors_api.py (endpoints + RBAC + pagination + ≤3 query budget + ETag on the vendor list + tenant isolation). Use the query_counter + ETag helpers.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema at the pg url, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; files <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md (one line) + tick PLAN 6.1. If you add to finance/queries.py or inventory/queries.py, note it as a sanctioned cross-module addition.

Return: files created/changed, the payment-terms + vendor-code modeling decisions, what you added to finance/inventory queries (if anything), test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, the §9 self-check, and deviations with one-line justification.

1	# SAP S/4HANA → Atlas Parity Map
2	
3	This document benchmarks Atlas ERP against SAP S/4HANA, the de-facto reference for enterprise ERP scope. Its purpose is twofold: to define what "complete" means for each functional area by enumerating the capabilities practitioners consider essential in current S/4HANA (2025/2026 releases), and to record — capability by capability — what Atlas v1 implements in full, what it implements in reduced form, and what it deliberately leaves out. The Atlas v1 scope is derived directly from this benchmark: every cut is documented with its rationale and an intended later path, so the gaps are commitments, not omissions. Research for this map was conducted in June 2026.
4	
5	**Methodology.** All twelve functional areas below were verified through live web research against current sources (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting publications); no area was built from the embedded knowledge baseline alone. Five areas — Financial Accounting, Inventory Management & Warehousing, Quality Management & Plant Maintenance, Project System, and Cross-cutting platform concepts — supplemented web findings with embedded S/4HANA knowledge for specific subtopics or where source pages could not be fetched; these are flagged in the Sources appendix.
6	
7	Reading the tables: capabilities that practitioners consider **essential** are shown in bold. The Notes column preserves, verbatim, the scoping rationale and the planned later path for every partial and out-of-scope capability — that record is the contract of this document.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Mandatory design inheritances
12	
13	Two S/4HANA architectural principles are hardcoded into Atlas and are non-negotiable across all modules:
14	
15	1. **Universal Journal pattern.** Atlas maintains one append-only financial line-item table as the single source of truth for all accounting data — the analogue of S/4HANA's ACDOCA. Every FI and CO view (trial balance, cost center report, margin analysis, financial statements) is a projection over this table. Totals are never separately stored; there are no aggregate tables to reconcile, and FI/CO reconciliation is eliminated by construction.
16	
17	2. **Document flow.** Every business document in Atlas records its predecessor and successor links (quote → order → delivery → invoice → journal entry, requisition → PO → goods receipt → supplier invoice, and so on), and the UI can render the full chain from any document in either direction — the analogue of S/4HANA's document flow and Document Relationship Browser.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Summary
22	
23	| S/4HANA area | Full | Partial | Out of scope | Total |
24	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
25	| Financial Accounting (FI) | 5 | 5 | 2 | 12 |
26	| Controlling (CO) | 4 | 4 | 3 | 11 |
27	| Procurement (MM-PUR) | 6 | 3 | 3 | 12 |
28	| Inventory Management & Warehousing (MM-IM / EWM) | 5 | 3 | 3 | 11 |
29	| Sales & Distribution (SD) | 2 | 6 | 4 | 12 |
30	| Production Planning (PP) | 4 | 3 | 5 | 12 |
31	| Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM) | 1 | 4 | 7 | 12 |
32	| Human Capital Management (HCM / SuccessFactors) | 5 | 5 | 2 | 12 |
33	| Project System (PS) | 2 | 2 | 8 | 12 |
34	| Cross-cutting platform concepts | 5 | 3 | 3 | 11 |
35	| Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics | 3 | 6 | 3 | 12 |
36	| Industry Solutions approach | 3 | 4 | 3 | 10 |
37	| **Total** | **45** | **48** | **46** | **139** |
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Financial Accounting (FI)
42	
43	SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting centers on the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), which merges general ledger, controlling, asset, and material-ledger line items into one multi-dimensional single source of truth, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation. Around that core sit Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, automatic payment runs), Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, dunning, incoming payments), Asset Accounting (ledger-based parallel valuation and depreciation), Bank and Cash Management, tax determination via tax codes and procedures, real-time financial statements drawn directly from the journal, and orchestrated period-end/year-end close. Distinctive S/4HANA traits practitioners flag as essential include parallel ledgers for multi-GAAP accounting, document splitting for dimension-complete balance sheets, up to 10 parallel currencies, and posting-period control.
44	
45	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| **General Ledger on the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)** | Full | finance | — |
48	| **Chart of accounts and fiscal year / posting period control** | Full | finance | — |
49	| **Multi-currency accounting and foreign currency valuation** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 (PLAN 4.3 done) has transaction + functional currency, a rates table (SPOT/CLOSING, direct-or-inverse lookup), posting-time translation with frozen functional amounts (largest-remainder residual balancing), purpose-keyed FX posting defaults, and an **unrealized**-FX revaluation run with auto-reversal. **Bounded out of v1:** group/additional parallel currencies; consolidation-style translation; **realized** FX (deferred to AP/AR clearing — purposes wired now); and **per-open-item** revaluation granularity — v1 revalues the per-account monetary foreign balance (accounts flagged `is_monetary` with a foreign `currency_code`), not individual uncleared AP/AR items. Later: add per-line extra currency columns + open-item-granular revaluation + realized FX at clearing, reusing the same rates-table and FX-account machinery. |
50	| **Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, payment runs, aging)** | Full | finance | Core AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging) is planned; bank payment file formats (ISO 20022/NACHA) and withholding tax are not explicitly in v1. Later: Layer payment-media file generation and withholding tax codes onto the existing payment-run engine. |
51	| **Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, receipts, dunning, aging)** | Full | finance | — |
52	| **Asset Accounting (parallel valuation, full lifecycle)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 is "asset accounting lite": register plus straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals; no parallel depreciation areas, transfers, retirements with gain/loss, revaluation, or assets under construction. Later: Extend the asset register with lifecycle events (transfer/retire/AuC settle) and per-ledger depreciation areas reusing the existing depreciation-run poster. |
53	| **Bank and Cash Management** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 covers bank reconciliation via CSV statement import with match suggestions only; no standard bank formats (MT940/CAMT), no auto-clearing rules engine, no cash positioning or liquidity forecasting. Later: Add MT940/CAMT.053 parsers feeding the same import pipeline, then a cash-position report over bank-clearing accounts. |
54	| **Tax handling (tax codes, determination, compliance reporting)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 plans line-level configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) — the calculation core — but no withholding tax, no statutory tax return reports, and no external tax engine integration. 63	
64	In current S/4HANA, Controlling is no longer a separate ledger world: FI and CO are merged into the Universal Journal (ACDOCA), so every posting carries cost center, profit center, project/WBS, order, and profitability-segment dimensions, and all CO reporting is a real-time projection of that single table; cost elements have become G/L accounts. Later: Build headcount/absence/labor-cost reports on the shared reporting module over HR and journal data. |

205	---
206	
207	## Project System (PS)
208	
209	S/4HANA Project System manages internal, capital-investment, and customer projects through hierarchical work breakdown structures (WBS) and optional networks/activities, covering structure planning, scheduling, cost and revenue planning, budgeting with availability control, execution postings (time via CATS, procurement, goods movements), and period-end close via settlement and results analysis / event-based revenue recognition. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026) the area spans classic PS (on-premise/private cloud) and the Fiori-based Enterprise Projects and Professional Services Projects in Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (public cloud). The Atlas v1 plan (WBS as costing objects, time and purchases postable to WBS, a project cost report) covers the execution-side core — structures and actual-cost collection — but deliberately omits the planning and financial-close layers: networks/scheduling, cost planning, budgeting/availability control, settlement, results analysis/revenue recognition, and customer-project billing are all out of scope for v1.
210	
211	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
212	|---|---|---|---|
213	| **Project definitions and WBS structures** | Full | projects | Later: Templates, status management, and mass-change tooling can be layered on the same WBS entity later. |
214	| **Networks, activities, and relationships** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 explicitly excludes networks; the v1 model is WBS-only cost collection with no activity/task layer. Later: Add an activity entity under WBS elements with relationships and confirmations, then attach scheduling and material components. |
215	| **Project scheduling and milestones** | Out of scope | — | Scheduling is explicitly not in the v1 list and depends on the network/activity layer, which is also excluded. Later: Introduce basic/forecast dates on WBS and activities plus a scheduling engine and Gantt view once networks exist. |
216	| **Project cost planning** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 collects only actual costs on WBS; no plan versions or planned-cost entry are in the plan, so the cost report has no plan/actual comparison. Later: Add a plan-cost table keyed by WBS element and period, then extend the project cost report to plan-vs-actual. |
217	| **Project budgeting and availability control** | Out of scope | — | Budgeting controls are explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 has no budget object and no posting-time funds check. Later: Add a budget amount per WBS with tolerance rules evaluated in the posting pipeline before actuals commit. |
218	| **Time recording to projects (CATS-style)** | Full | projects | Later: Approval workflows and posting to network activities can follow once those features exist. |
219	| **Procurement and expense postings to projects** | Partial | projects | Atlas v1 plans actual purchase and expense postings to WBS, but PR/PO commitment tracking and project stock / project MRP are not planned. Later: Derive commitment records from open purchase orders assigned to WBS, then add project-stock segments in inventory. |
220	| **Project settlement** | Out of scope | — | Settlement is explicitly excluded from v1; collected costs remain on the WBS with no period-end transfer to receivers. Later: Add settlement rules per WBS and a periodic settlement run reusing the finance allocation/posting engine. |
221	| **Results analysis / event-based revenue recognition** | Out of scope | — | No revenue recognition or WIP/POC valuation of project costs is planned in v1; v1 projects are pure cost collectors. Later: Implement event-based recognition postings in the finance module triggered by project cost and billing events. |
222	| **Customer project billing integration** | Out of scope | — | Not in the v1 list; there is no planned sales-order-to-WBS link or billing generated from project time/expenses. Later: Link sales order lines to WBS elements, then generate resource-related billing proposals from posted time and expenses. |
223	| **Project cost reporting and analytics** | Partial | projects | v1 plans a project cost report over actuals by WBS, but without plan or commitment columns and without the broader drilldown/overview suite, it is a reduced subset. Later: Extend the report with commitment and plan columns and line-item drilldown as those data objects are added. |
224	| Progress analysis / earned value management | Out of scope | — | Depends on cost planning, budgets, and scheduling, none of which are in v1; also not considered core by most practitioners outside EPC/engineering industries. Later: Compute POC and earned value from plan-cost and confirmation data once planning and scheduling layers exist. |
225	
226	---
227	
228	## Cross-cutting platform concepts
229	
230	Cross-cutting platform concepts in S/4HANA (2025/2026) are the architectural primitives every functional module relies on: the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as the single financial line-item table; document flow with predecessor/successor links viewable in the Document Relationship Browser; the mandatory unified Business Partner model (CVI-synchronized customer/vendor views); the BRF+/Adobe Forms output management framework; configurable number ranges per document type; the roles/profiles authorization concept (PFCG on-premise, business roles with restrictions in Cloud); and the client (MANDT) field on nearly every table on-premise, replaced by tenant isolation in S/4HANA Cloud SaaS. Atlas v1 deliberately inherits the two load-bearing patterns (Universal Journal, document flow) and covers tenancy, RBAC, audit, and numbering, while consciously deviating on the Business Partner model and deferring output management, workflow, and extensibility.
231	
232	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
233	|---|---|---|---|
234	| **Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as single source of truth** | Full | finance | — |
235	| **Document flow / Document Relationship Browser** | Full | core | — |
236	| **Unified Business Partner model (BP + CVI)** | Partial | core | Deliberate deviation: Atlas v1 keeps separate vendor and customer master tables; customer/vendor master data itself is planned, but there is no unified party object, no shared roles/relationships, and no single identity for an entity that is both customer and supplier. Later: Introduce a thin party/business-partner table that links existing customer and vendor records as roles, without restructuring the two masters. |
237	| **Output management (determination rules, channels, form templates)** | Partial | core | Atlas v1 plans only basic document rendering; the rule-based determination framework, multi-channel dispatch (email/EDI), template management, and output status/retry queue are explicitly not in the v1 list. Later: Add a rule-driven output determination service (document attributes → channel + template + recipient) with pluggable channel adapters and a retryable output queue. |
238	| **Number ranges (document numbering)** | Full | core | Later: Add external number assignment and per-fiscal-year ranges later if conversion/legal scenarios demand them. |
239	| **Authorization concept (roles, profiles, restrictions)** | Partial | admin | Atlas v1 plans the RBAC core (JWT auth, roles → permissions → resources stored as data), but S/4HANA's field/org-value restrictions (scoping a permission to specific company codes, plants, etc.) and segregation-of-duties analysis are not in the v1 list. Later: Extend permission records with attribute/scope filters (org-unit values) evaluated alongside the tenant filter, then layer SoD rule checks on role assignments. |
240	| **Multi-client architecture / SaaS multi-tenancy** | Full | core | — |
241	| **Audit trail / change documents** | Full | core | Later: Add read-access logging for sensitive fields as a later compliance increment. |
242	| **Extensibility framework (custom fields, key-user and side-by-side extensions)** | Out of scope | — | No custom-field or extension mechanism appears anywhere in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 ships fixed schemas only. Later: Add JSONB custom-field columns with metadata-driven validation on core entities, plus webhook/event hooks per document type. |
243	| **Workflow engine (flexible approval workflows)** | Out of scope | — | No approval/workflow capability is in the Atlas v1 plan; documents post directly without configurable release strategies, which practitioners consider a core control in procurement and finance. Later: Add a generic approval service (document type + condition → ordered approver steps) driving a status field that blocks posting until approved. |
244	| **Released APIs and event-based integration** | Out of scope | — | The Atlas v1 cross-cutting scope defines internal patterns (journal, flow, tenancy, auth) but lists no public API contract or event emission for external integration. Later: Publish the existing internal REST endpoints as a versioned public API and emit domain events (document created/changed) to a message bus or webhooks. |

247	
248	## Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics
249	
250	In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), this area covers the Fiori design system (Horizon theme, SAPUI5/Fiori elements controls), the role-based launchpad organized into spaces and pages with app/KPI/insight tiles, standard floorplans (list report, object page, overview page, analytical list page, worklist), and embedded analytics built on the CDS virtual data model: analytical queries, Smart Business KPI tiles with thresholds and drill-down, multidimensional reports, and self-service query creation — all running live on transactional data with insight-to-action navigation into transactions. The 2025 release adds Fiori 4.0 touches: AI-assisted enterprise search, Joule integration, smart summarization, and AI-personalized My Home insight cards. Atlas v1 covers the essential core of the role-based home page, role dashboards, and tabular self-service reporting; it plans reduced subsets of the component library, floorplan patterns, semantic layer, KPI framework, and drill-down analytics; and it omits enterprise search, per-user personalization/variants, and AI-assisted UX entirely.
251	
252	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
253	|---|---|---|---|
254	| **Role-based launchpad home with spaces/pages and app/KPI tiles** | Full | frontend | — |
255	| **Fiori design system and UI component library (Horizon, SAPUI5 controls)** | Partial | frontend | Atlas plans a focused in-house kit (data grid, form builder, kanban, dashboard cards, document-flow viewer), not a full design system with theming tokens, accessibility standards, and the breadth of SAPUI5 controls. Later: Grow the kit into a documented design system: theme tokens, a11y audit, and new controls added as app screens demand them. |
256	| **List report + object page floorplans (transactional work pattern)** | Partial | frontend | Atlas's data grid and form builder cover hand-built list+detail screens, but there is no metadata-driven floorplan generator, draft persistence, or saved table variants. Later: Add a schema-driven page generator that renders list+detail CRUD pages from entity metadata, then layer in drafts and variants. |
257	| **Overview pages / role-based dashboards** | Full | reporting | — |
258	| **Analytical list page and multidimensional reporting** | Partial | reporting | Atlas's report builder yields a flat group-by grid with CSV export; no interactive pivoting, drill-down paths, or combined chart+table analysis UI is planned. Later: Add a pivot/drill-down UI and chart rendering on top of existing report-builder queries. |
259	| **CDS virtual data model and analytical queries (live semantic layer)** | Partial | reporting | Atlas's report builder queries raw entities directly, which preserves the live-on-transactional-data principle, but there is no reusable layered view model, calculated/restricted measures, or hierarchies. Later: Introduce a versioned semantic layer (named reusable views and measures) that the report builder, dashboards, and KPI tiles all consume. |
260	| **Smart Business KPI framework (Manage KPIs and Reports)** | Partial | reporting | Atlas ships a fixed set of KPI tiles and dashboard cards; end-user KPI authoring, threshold/target rules, color states, and publish-to-home are not planned. Later: Add a "manage KPIs" admin screen where a KPI = saved report query + threshold rules, publishable as a home-page tile. |
261	| **Self-service query creation and export (Query Browser, custom analytical queries)** | Full | reporting | — |
262	| **Insight-to-action and intent-based cross-app navigation** | Partial | frontend | Atlas plans a document-flow viewer component, but no generic deep-link/intent framework wiring dashboard cards and report rows to the owning app screens. Later: Define per-entity URL route conventions (deep links) and wire dashboard cards, KPI tiles, and report rows to them. |
263	| **Enterprise search across business objects** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 plans only per-report filters; no global cross-entity search or app finder exists anywhere in the plan. Later: Add a global search endpoint over key entities plus a header omnibox that deep-links into list/detail pages. |
264	| **Personalization and key-user UI adaptation** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 home pages, dashboards, and grids are role-defined and static; no per-user variants, tile rearrangement, or screen adaptation is planned. Later: Persist per-user grid/filter variants and home-tile layout as JSON preference records keyed by user and screen. |
265	| Joule and AI-assisted UX (NL navigation, smart summarization, easy filter) | Out of scope | — | Flagship 2025 differentiator but not yet baseline-essential, and largely premium/optional even in S/4HANA; nothing AI-related is in the Atlas v1 plan. Later: Once report-builder and search APIs exist, attach an LLM assistant that translates natural language into report definitions and deep links. |

268	
269	## Industry Solutions approach
270	
271	SAP's S/4HANA industry approach folded most former IS add-ons into a single codebase ("industry to core"), covering roughly 25 industries whose functionality is activated per system through business function sets and the switch framework — activation is largely irreversible, one industry function set per instance, and industry-specific LoB functions are licensed separately from the Enterprise Management core. What the industry layer actually varies is substantial: terminology (Article vs Material, Site vs Plant), industry master data models (retail article/site, patient, equipment), entire vertical process suites (merchandise management, EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management, IS-U billing), regulatory content, and preconfigured SAP Best Practices content applied at setup. The current 2025/2026 direction adds a clean-core posture where deep vertical needs increasingly move to SAP Industry Cloud partner extensions on BTP — notably SAP is discontinuing healthcare IS-H by 2030 in favor of partner solutions. Atlas v1's YAML template layer maps well to the configuration-content slice of this area but plans none of the vertical process logic, industry master data objects, regulatory content, or partner extension ecosystem that practitioners associate with SAP industry solutions.
272	
273	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
274	|---|---|---|---|
275	| **Single-core delivery with industry activation (business function sets / switch framework)** | Partial | industry | Atlas templates toggle modules and apply presets at tenant creation, but there is no deep switch layer that changes the behavior of shared module code per industry (e.g., retail switch altering core MM logistics flows). Later: Add a feature-flag/behavior-variant layer inside modules keyed off the tenant's industry template. |
276	| **Industry-specific terminology overrides** | Full | industry | — |
277	| **Industry-specific master data models** | Partial | industry | Typed custom fields (JSONB + metadata registry) extend core entities, but Atlas v1 plans no first-class industry entities such as article variant matrices, store hierarchies, or a patient demographics object. Later: Ship industry entities as optional modules built on the metadata registry, starting with retail article/site. |
278	| **Industry-specific end-to-end business processes** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 templates only configure existing horizontal modules; no industry-specific process logic of any kind is planned. Later: Post-v1 industry process packs as optional modules layered on core (e.g., a retail pack adding assortment/promotion flows). |
279	| **Preconfigured industry best-practice content applied at provisioning** | Full | industry | — |
280	| **Metadata-driven field extensibility surfaced across the UI** | Full | core | — |
281	| **Industry regulatory and statutory compliance** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 templates carry only default tax codes; no industry- or country-specific statutory logic, regulated billing, or POC revenue recognition is planned in the industry layer. Later: Country/industry compliance packs per module once a localization framework exists, prioritized by shipped templates. |
282	| **Breadth of industry coverage (~25 verticals)** | Partial | industry | Atlas v1 ships 5 templates (manufacturing, retail, professional-services, healthcare, construction); deep verticals like utilities, banking, or oil & gas need far more than configuration templates. Later: Grow template coverage via community-contributed YAML templates, pairing deep verticals with later process-pack modules. |
283	| **Partner and industry-cloud extension ecosystem** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 plans no plugin/extension API or marketplace through which third parties could ship industry functionality; templates are first-party YAML only. Later: Define a stable plugin API plus template packaging so third parties can publish installable industry packs. |
284	| **Lifecycle-safe industry configuration management** | Partial | industry | Idempotent template application at tenant creation is planned, but there is no template versioning or safe re-application/upgrade of templates to existing live tenants. Later: Version templates and add a migration-aware re-apply command that diffs template state against live tenant config. |

1	"""Inventory's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Inventory sits just above finance in the dependency order: every module above it (procurement,
4	sales, manufacturing) may import THIS file to read inventory state synchronously, and inventory
5	imports only finance/queries downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is
6	the ONLY inventory file other modules import.
7	
8	For PLAN 5.1 it exposes the item-master reads those modules will need: existence checks, the
9	item's base UoM and costing method, and the category's GL-account wiring (so the COGS handler can
10	resolve where to post when stock issues land in 5.2+). PLAN 5.2 adds the ON-HAND projection reads
11	(``total_on_hand``, ``on_hand_by_bin``, ``on_hand_by_lot``) — what sales ATP and procurement will
12	call: they read the MAINTAINED ``inv_stock_quants`` projection (D-036), an indexed aggregate, never
13	an unbounded SUM over the move history (PERFORMANCE §1).
14	
15	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
16	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
17	"""

97	# --- On-hand projection reads (PLAN 5.2) --------------------------------------
98	# These read the MAINTAINED inv_stock_quants projection (D-036), kept in lock-step with the move
99	# ledger so on-hand is an indexed aggregate over a small current-state table, not a SUM over
100	# unbounded move history (PERFORMANCE §1). MoneyType/QuantityType propagation keeps the SUM exact on
101	# both engines (D-015); ``func.coalesce(..., 0)`` makes an item with no stock read 0, not None.

104	async def total_on_hand(

106	) -> Decimal:

108	    starts from. Reads inv_stock_quants (the maintained projection), index-served by
109	    ``(tenant_id, item_id)``."""
110	    stmt = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty), 0)).where(

116	async def on_hand(
117	    session: AsyncSession,
118	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
119	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
120	    bin_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
121	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
122	) -> Decimal:
123	    """On-hand quantity of an item, optionally narrowed to one bin and/or one lot (PLAN 5.2). With
124	    no bin/lot this is ``total_on_hand``; with a bin it is that bin's stock; with a lot it is that
125	    lot's stock (in the bin if also given). Reads the maintained projection."""
126	    stmt = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty), 0)).where(
127	        StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockQuant.item_id == item_id
128	    )
129	    if bin_id is not None:
130	        stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.bin_id == bin_id)
131	    if lot_id is not None:
132	        stmt = stmt.where(StockQuant.lot_id == lot_id)
133	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()

136	async def on_hand_by_bin(
137	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
138	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
139	    """Per-bin on-hand totals for an item (PLAN 5.2): ``{bin_id: qty}`` summed across that bin's
140	    lots. Bins with zero net stock are absent (the move service deletes a quant when it hits 0, so
141	    the projection holds only live stock). What a bin-level stock-overview screen reads."""
142	    stmt = (
143	        select(StockQuant.bin_id, func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty))
144	        .where(StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id, StockQuant.item_id == item_id)

146	    )
147	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()

151	async def on_hand_by_lot(
152	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
153	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
154	    """Per-lot on-hand totals for a LOT-tracked item (PLAN 5.2): ``{lot_id: qty}`` summed across
155	    bins. Quants with a NULL lot (fungible stock) are excluded — this view is for tracked items
156	    where lot traceability matters."""
157	    stmt = (
158	        select(StockQuant.lot_id, func.sum(StockQuant.on_hand_qty))
159	        .where(
160	            StockQuant.tenant_id == tenant_id,
161	            StockQuant.item_id == item_id,
162	            StockQuant.lot_id.is_not(None),
163	        )
164	        .group_by(StockQuant.lot_id)
165	    )
166	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
167	    return {row[0]: row[1] for row in rows}

170	# --- Valuation reads (PLAN 5.3, D-020/D-037) ----------------------------------
171	# These read the VALUE SSOT (inv_item_valuations for moving-average, inv_cost_layers for FIFO), kept
172	# in lock-step with every move in the same transaction (D-037). The inventory-value dashboard KPI
173	# and
174	# valuation reports read these. MoneyType/QuantityType propagation keeps the SUMs exact (D-015).
175	
176	
177	async def item_value(
178	    session: AsyncSession,
179	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
180	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
181	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
182	) -> Decimal:
183	    """The current total inventory VALUE of an item (PLAN 5.3), optionally narrowed to one
184	    warehouse.
185	
186	    For a MOVING_AVERAGE item this sums ``inv_item_valuations.total_value``; for a FIFO item it sums
187	    ``remaining_qty × unit_cost`` over the live cost layers. An item uses exactly one method, so the
188	    other source contributes 0. The FIFO product is summed in PYTHON (each factor already a typed
189	    Decimal) rather than ``func.sum(qty × cost)``, because multiplying two scaled-integer columns on
190	    SQLite yields a ×10^12 value that the MoneyType result processor cannot un-scale (D-015 trigger
191	    discipline: SQL never multiplies two stored money/quantity columns)."""
192	    valuation_stmt = select(
193	        func.coalesce(func.sum(ItemValuation.total_value), 0)
194	    ).where(ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id, ItemValuation.item_id == item_id)
195	    layer_stmt = select(CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
196	        CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id,
197	        CostLayer.item_id == item_id,
198	        CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0,
199	    )
200	    if warehouse_id is not None:
201	        valuation_stmt = valuation_stmt.where(ItemValuation.warehouse_id == warehouse_id)
202	        layer_stmt = layer_stmt.where(CostLayer.warehouse_id == warehouse_id)
203	    mav_value = Decimal((await session.execute(valuation_stmt)).scalar_one())
204	    fifo_value = sum(
205	        (Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost) for qty, cost in (await session.execute(layer_stmt)).all()),
206	        Decimal(0),
207	    )
208	    return mav_value + fifo_value
209	
210	
211	async def valuation_summary(
212	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
213	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
214	    """Total inventory value per item across the tenant (PLAN 5.3): ``{item_id: value}`` — the
215	    moving-average totals plus the FIFO live-layer values, merged per item. What the inventory-value
216	    dashboard KPI sums. The moving-average totals are grouped in SQL; the FIFO layer products are
217	    summed in Python per item (D-015: no SQL multiply of two scaled money/quantity columns).
218	    PERFORMANCE §6: two reads, no per-item N+1."""
219	    mav_rows = (
220	        await session.execute(
221	            select(ItemValuation.item_id, func.sum(ItemValuation.total_value))
222	            .where(ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id)
223	            .group_by(ItemValuation.item_id)
224	        )
225	    ).all()
226	    layer_rows = (
227	        await session.execute(
228	            select(CostLayer.item_id, CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
229	                CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id, CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0
230	            )
231	        )
232	    ).all()
233	    totals: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
234	    for item_id_, value in mav_rows:
235	        if value is not None:
236	            totals[item_id_] = totals.get(item_id_, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(value)
237	    for item_id_, qty, cost in layer_rows:
238	        totals[item_id_] = totals.get(item_id_, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost)
239	    return totals
240	
241	
242	async def current_unit_cost(
243	    session: AsyncSession,
244	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
245	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
246	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID,
247	) -> Decimal:
248	    """The item's current per-unit BOOK cost in a warehouse (PLAN 5.4): the moving-average
249	    ``avg_unit_cost`` for a MOVING_AVERAGE item, or the weighted average of the live FIFO layers for
250	    a FIFO item — the SAME source a value-neutral transfer uses for its ledger cost
251	    (costing._current_unit_cost). A positive count variance enters stock at this cost so the value
252	    added matches the book cost (rather than an arbitrary entry price). Returns 0 when no
253	    valuation/layer exists yet (an item the system thinks is empty, counted positive — the
254	    adjustment then enters at 0 cost, a quantity-only correction with no value impact, which the
255	    operator can re-cost via a later receipt). The FIFO layer product is summed in PYTHON (D-015: no
256	    SQL multiply of two scaled money/quantity columns). One read for the MAV row, one for the FIFO
257	    layers (no per-layer N+1)."""
258	    valuation = (
259	        await session.execute(
260	            select(ItemValuation.avg_unit_cost).where(
261	                ItemValuation.tenant_id == tenant_id,
262	                ItemValuation.item_id == item_id,
263	                ItemValuation.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
264	            )
265	        )
266	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
267	    if valuation is not None:
268	        return Decimal(valuation)
269	    rows = (
270	        await session.execute(
271	            select(CostLayer.remaining_qty, CostLayer.unit_cost).where(
272	                CostLayer.tenant_id == tenant_id,
273	                CostLayer.item_id == item_id,
274	                CostLayer.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
275	                CostLayer.remaining_qty > 0,
276	            )
277	        )
278	    ).all()
279	    total_qty = sum((Decimal(qty) for qty, _cost in rows), Decimal(0))
280	    total_value = sum((Decimal(qty) * Decimal(cost) for qty, cost in rows), Decimal(0))
281	    return (total_value / total_qty) if total_qty > 0 else Decimal(0)

2

4	may import THIS file to read finance state synchronously, and finance imports no other

7	inventory/sales call ``get_period_status`` to refuse stock/sales documents dated into a closed
8	period before they reach the GL.

11	the D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — these are ordinary tenant-scoped
12	ORM reads, not a bypass.

44	async def find_period_for_date(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, on_date: date
46	) -> FiscalPeriod | None:
47	    """The fiscal period whose [start_date, end_date] (inclusive) covers ``on_date``, or
48	    None if no period does. Periods within a year are contiguous and non-overlapping (the
49	    service enforces that on generation), so at most one matches. This is the date->period
50	    lookup the journal uses on every posting (4.2)."""
51	    stmt = select(FiscalPeriod).where(
52	        FiscalPeriod.tenant_id == tenant_id,
53	        FiscalPeriod.start_date <= on_date,

65	    (the DB-level period trigger on the journal in 4.2 is the bypass-proof backstop)."""

159	    is the bottom of the dependency order (STRUCTURE §5). Keyed by the opaque ``partner_id``; never

211	    bottom-dependency contract (STRUCTURE §5). Sums in Python over the (typically small) open set so

221	async def cost_center_exists(
222	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID
223	) -> bool:
224	    """Whether a cost centre with ``cost_center_id`` exists in the tenant. The journal posting flow
225	    calls this to validate a line's ``cost_center_id`` dimension before the line is written —
226	    service-level dimension integrity replacing the absent FK on the trigger-bearing journal-lines
227	    table (D-022)."""
228	    stmt = select(CostCenter.id).where(
229	        CostCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id, CostCenter.id == cost_center_id
230	    )

235	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, profit_center_id: uuid.UUID
236	) -> bool:
237	    """Whether a profit centre with ``profit_center_id`` exists in the tenant. The companion to
238	    ``cost_center_exists`` for the journal line's ``profit_center_id`` dimension (D-022)."""
239	    stmt = select(ProfitCenter.id).where(
240	        ProfitCenter.tenant_id == tenant_id, ProfitCenter.id == profit_center_id
241	    )
242	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None

245	async def cost_center_balance(
246	    session: AsyncSession,
247	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
248	    cost_center_id: uuid.UUID,
249	    period_id: uuid.UUID,
250	) -> Decimal:
251	    """The cost centre's NET functional balance for a fiscal period (PLAN 4.7): SUM over POSTED
252	    journal lines carrying this ``cost_center_id`` in ``period_id`` of (functional debit minus
253	    functional credit). This is the amount ``run_allocation`` redistributes — CO is a projection of
254	    the journal (D-021), so the balance is derived from journal lines, never a stored total.
255	    MoneyType type propagation keeps the SUM exact on both engines (D-015); returns 0 when none."""
256	    debit = func.coalesce(
257	        func.sum(JournalLine.functional_debit_amount), 0
258	    )
259	    credit = func.coalesce(
260	        func.sum(JournalLine.functional_credit_amount), 0
261	    )
262	    stmt = select(debit - credit).where(
263	        JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
264	        JournalLine.cost_center_id == cost_center_id,
265	        JournalLine.fiscal_period_id == period_id,
266	        JournalLine.is_posted.is_(True),
267	    )
268	    result = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one()
269	    return Decimal(str(result)) if result is not None else Decimal(0)
270

272	# --- Statements: the base aggregate, exposed for reporting reuse (PLAN 4.8, D-021) -----------
273	
274	
275	async def account_balances(
276	    session: AsyncSession,
277	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
278	    *,
279	    date_to: date,
280	    date_from: date | None = None,
281	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
282	    """Signed (debit-positive) net balance per account over the posted journal (D-021). The single
283	    statement base aggregate, exposed here so the reporting module (PLAN 13) builds its own views as
284	    projections of the SAME query the statements use — never a stored total. ``date_from`` bounds
285	    the range (a P&L-style window); omit it for cumulative-to-date balances (balance-sheet-style).
286	    Thin re-export of ``service.statements._account_balances`` — one aggregate, one index."""
287	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements import _account_balances
288	
289	    return await _account_balances(
290	        session, tenant_id, date_to=date_to, date_from=date_from
291	    )
292	
293	
294	async def net_income(
295	    session: AsyncSession,
296	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
297	    *,
298	    date_to: date,
299	    date_from: date | None = None,
300	) -> Decimal:
301	    """Net income (revenue - expense, credit-positive so a profit is positive) over the range
302	    (D-021). Derived from ``account_balances`` + account types so reporting reads it as a projection
303	    of the journal — the same figure the balance sheet folds into retained earnings. Cumulative to
304	    ``date_to`` when ``date_from`` is omitted."""
305	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements import net_income_signed
306	    from app.modules.finance.service.statements.base import load_account_meta
307	
308	    balances = await account_balances(
309	        session, tenant_id, date_to=date_to, date_from=date_from
310	    )
311	    meta = await load_account_meta(session, tenant_id)
312	    return net_income_signed(balances, meta)

1	"""Accounts Payable: vendor bills, payments and payment allocations (PLAN 4.5, D-029).
2	
3	The AP sub-ledger is keyed by an OPAQUE ``partner_id`` (D-029): finance is the bottom of the
4	dependency order, so it never FK-references a vendor master (that lives in procurement, above
5	finance). Each AP document carries the opaque ``partner_id`` plus a denormalized ``partner_name``
6	for display; the owning module guarantees the id. Open items (the amount still owed on a bill)
7	live in ``open_amount`` on the bill, reduced as payments allocate against it.
8	
9	Every AP document posts through the universal journal (D-017): a ``VendorBill`` registers in
10	core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin) and gets a ``journal_entry_id`` + system number at
11	posting; a ``VendorPayment`` is created and posted in one step, clearing the open items its
12	allocations name. Realized FX at clearing (D-019) is computed in the SERVICE, posted inside the
13	payment journal entry — no extra columns here.
14	
15	Fifth file in the finance ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3); re-exported from ``models/__init__``.
16	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015, exact on both engines). All cross-row links are composite
17	tenant FKs (D-007 backstop) EXCEPT ``partner_id`` (opaque, no FK — D-029) and the dimension ids.
18	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum value, as elsewhere in finance.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from datetime import date
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
26	
27	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
28	from app.core.models import (
29	    AuditMixin,
30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	    tenant_unique,
36	)
37	from app.core.money import MoneyType
38	from app.modules.finance.constants import BillStatus, PaymentStatus
39	
40	
41	class VendorBill(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
42	    """A vendor bill / supplier invoice (PLAN 4.5). Registered in core_documents at creation
43	    (DocumentMixin, doc_number NULL); the gapless system ``bill_number`` is claimed at POSTING
44	    (D-012). ``partner_id`` is the OPAQUE vendor id (D-029 — no FK); ``partner_name`` is the
45	    denormalized display name. ``bill_external_ref`` is the vendor's own document number (free
46	    text, not unique). At posting the service builds the AP journal entry (Dr expense/asset lines +
47	    Dr input tax, Cr AP control gross), sets ``journal_entry_id`` + ``open_amount`` = gross, and
48	    flips ``status`` to POSTED. ``open_amount`` (transaction currency) is the still-owed balance,
49	    reduced by payment allocations until PAID. Audited (D-010): a financial document."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "fin_vendor_bills"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        tenant_unique(),
54	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
55	        document_fk(),
56	        # The AP control account this bill credits (composite tenant FK). Bills carry their own
57	        # AP control account so the sub-ledger needs no fixed default (D-029).
58	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "ap_account_id"),
59	        # The journal entry created at posting (composite tenant FK; NULL until posted).
60	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
61	        # Hot-list filter combination for GET /vendor-bills, aging, and payment runs
62	        # (PERFORMANCE §1, #25): tenant leads, then the dominant filters, then the sort key.
63	        sa.Index(
64	            "ix_fin_vendor_bills_list_filters",
65	            "tenant_id",
66	            "partner_id",
67	            "status",
68	            "bill_date",
69	        ),
70	    )
71	
72	    partner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
73	    partner_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
74	    # The vendor's own reference on the bill (free text, not the system number); nullable.
75	    bill_external_ref: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
76	    # The gapless system number, claimed at posting (NULL until then; D-012).
77	    bill_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
78	    bill_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
79	    due_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
80	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
81	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
82	        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=BillStatus.DRAFT.value, server_default="DRAFT"
83	    )
84	    ap_account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
85	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
86	    gross_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
87	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
88	    )
89	    tax_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
90	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
91	    )
92	    net_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
93	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
94	    )
95	    # Still-owed balance in the bill's transaction currency. Equals gross at posting; reduced by
96	    # payment allocations until 0 (PAID). No stored total elsewhere — aging projects over this.
97	    open_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
98	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
99	    )
100	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
101	
102	
103	class VendorBillLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
104	    """One expense/asset line on a vendor bill (PLAN 4.5). ``account_id`` is the GL account the net
105	    debits at posting; ``tax_code_id`` (nullable) drives the input-tax calculation, with the
106	    resulting ``tax_amount`` posted to the tax code's receivable account. ``cost_center_id`` and
107	    ``project_id`` are opaque CO/project dimensions (no FK — masters land in later phases, mirroring
108	    the journal line). NOT AuditMixin: lines are written once with their bill and the bill's audit
109	    row records the document-level change (same exclusion as journal lines)."""
110	
111	    __tablename__ = "fin_vendor_bill_lines"
112	    __table_args__ = (
113	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
114	            "tenant_id",
115	            "bill_id",
116	            "line_number",
117	            name="uq_fin_vendor_bill_lines_tenant_id_bill_id_line_number",
118	        ),
119	        tenant_unique(),
120	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
121	        tenant_fk("fin_vendor_bills", "bill_id"),
122	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "account_id"),
123	        tenant_fk("fin_tax_codes", "tax_code_id"),
124	    )
125	
126	    bill_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
127	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
128	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
129	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
130	    net_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
131	    tax_code_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
132	    tax_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
133	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
134	    )
135	    cost_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
136	    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)

139	class VendorPayment(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
140	    """A vendor payment (PLAN 4.5). Created and posted in one step: the service builds the payment
141	    journal entry (Dr AP control for the sum cleared, Cr bank for ``amount``, plus a realized-FX
142	    gain/loss line when the bill rate differs from the payment rate, D-019), then claims the gapless
143	    ``payment_number`` (D-012) and links the payment to the bills it clears. ``partner_id`` is the
144	    OPAQUE vendor id (D-029); ``bank_account_id`` is the bank/cash account credited. Audited
145	    (D-010). The bills cleared and by how much live in ``VendorPaymentAllocation`` rows."""
146	
147	    __tablename__ = "fin_vendor_payments"
148	    __table_args__ = (
149	        tenant_unique(),
150	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
151	        document_fk(),
152	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "bank_account_id"),
153	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
154	    )
155	
156	    partner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
157	    partner_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
158	    payment_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
159	    payment_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
160	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
161	    bank_account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
162	    amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)
163	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
164	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
165	        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=PaymentStatus.POSTED.value, server_default="POSTED"
166	    )
167	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)

170	class VendorPaymentAllocation(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
171	    """One (payment -> bill) clearing allocation (PLAN 4.5): how much of a payment cleared a given
172	    bill, in the transaction currency. UNIQUE(tenant_id, payment_id, vendor_bill_id) so a payment
173	    clears each bill at most once. NOT AuditMixin: an allocation is written once with its payment
174	    and the payment's audit row records the document-level change."""

176	    __tablename__ = "fin_vendor_payment_allocations"
177	    __table_args__ = (
178	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
179	            "tenant_id",
180	            "payment_id",
181	            "vendor_bill_id",
182	            # Short explicit name: PG caps identifiers at 63 chars and does NOT truncate explicit
183	            # names (the D-022 column-0 convention would otherwise collide with tenant_unique()).
184	            name="uq_fin_vendor_payment_allocations_payment_bill",
185	        ),
186	        tenant_unique(),
187	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
188	        tenant_fk("fin_vendor_payments", "payment_id"),
189	        tenant_fk("fin_vendor_bills", "vendor_bill_id"),

192	    payment_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
193	    vendor_bill_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
194	    allocated_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=False)

59	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
60	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow, returning its ORM result refreshed in the async
61	    context so a sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (twin of finance _commit)."""
62	    holder: list[T] = []
63	
64	    async def _work() -> None:
65	        result = await work()
66	        await session.refresh(result)
67	        holder.append(result)
68	
69	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
70	    return holder[0]

1	"""Inventory master data (PLAN 5.1): item categories, UoMs, per-item UoM conversions, the item
2	master, and the lot/serial instance tables.
3	
4	One file in the ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3: the combined models.py was split into a
5	models/ package when PLAN 5.2's warehouse/bin/move/quant tables would have pushed it over the
6	400-line cap, the finance models/ precedent). This file owns the 5.1 MASTER tables; the 5.2
7	warehouse/bin/move/quant STOCK tables live in ``models/stock.py``.
8	
9	Design decisions baked in here:
10	
11	- **Costing wiring on the category (D-020 + D-029).** ``ItemCategory`` carries the default
12	  costing method AND the three GL accounts COGS/valuation posting will need —
13	  ``inventory_account_id``, ``cogs_account_id``, ``price_difference_account_id`` — as OPAQUE
14	  ``sa.Uuid`` columns, NOT cross-module FKs (D-029): finance owns those accounts; the inventory
15	  service validates each id exists via ``finance/queries.py`` when set, and the journal-line
16	  precedent already stores finance dimension ids without an FK on a cross-module table. They are
17	  NULLABLE on the category (a SERVICE-only category needs none); a STOCKED item's category must
18	  carry them before that item can post moves — validated when moves land (5.2+), not in 5.1.
19	
20	- **costing_method on the item (D-020).** Defaulted from the category at create but STORED on the
21	  item, because the item is the costing unit and D-020 lets it change only while no stock exists.
22	
23	- **UoM convention (the chosen one of the two the task offered): per-item BASE + ALTERNATES.**
24	  Each item has ONE ``base_uom_id``; quantities are stored/costed in the base UoM. An
25	  ``UomConversion`` row expresses an ALTERNATE UoM for that item as ``factor_to_base`` —
26	  multiplying a quantity in the alternate UoM by the factor yields the base-UoM quantity (an
27	  item whose base is EA and has BOX with factor 12 means 1 BOX = 12 EA). ``UNIQUE(tenant_id,
28	  item_id, alt_uom_id)`` — one factor per (item, alternate). This is the standard ERP shape
29	  (S/4HANA's alternative-UoM table): simpler than a full from/to graph, and base<->alt and
30	  alt<->alt conversions all derive from the single per-alternate factor (service.convert_quantity).
31	
32	- **Lot / SerialNumber are MASTER tables only for 5.1.** They are defined so the schema is
33	  receipt-ready, but instances are CREATED during receipts (5.2+); 5.1 ships no CRUD for them.
34	
35	All tables follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop: ``tenant_unique()`` on every table
36	referenced by a child, ``tenant_fk()`` composites for every cross-row link so a child can never
37	point at another tenant's parent. Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the
38	StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the core/finance convention, no ``sa.Enum``); the service maps
39	to/from the constants classes.
40	"""

1	"""Item business logic (PLAN 5.1, D-020): CRUD + type/tracking/costing validation.
2	
3	Rules enforced here: item_code uniqueness (friendly ConflictError before the DB UNIQUE would
4	raise); category + base UoM exist; costing_method defaults from the category when omitted (D-020),
5	stored on the item; tracking only on STOCKED items. ``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps
6	``Page[Item]`` (the ORM model) a string at import; the router re-validates page items.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import uuid
12	
13	from sqlalchemy import select
14	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
15	
16	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
17	from app.core.pagination import OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
18	from app.core.schemas import Page
19	from app.modules.inventory.constants import CostingMethod, ItemType, TrackingMode
20	from app.modules.inventory.models import Item
21	from app.modules.inventory.schemas import ItemCreate, ItemFilter, ItemUpdate
22	from app.modules.inventory.service.categories import get_category
23	from app.modules.inventory.service.uoms import get_uom
24	
25	
26	def _resolve_tracking(item_type: ItemType, tracking_mode: TrackingMode) -> None:
27	    """Enforce "tracking only on STOCKED items" (D-020): a NON_STOCKED/SERVICE item must keep
28	    tracking_mode = NONE — those types carry no stock to track."""
29	    if item_type != ItemType.STOCKED and tracking_mode != TrackingMode.NONE:
30	        raise ValidationFailedError(
31	            message="Only stocked items can be lot- or serial-tracked",
32	            code="inventory.tracking_requires_stocked",
33	            details={"item_type": item_type.value, "tracking_mode": tracking_mode.value},
34	        )
35	
36	
37	async def get_item(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID) -> Item:
38	    item = await session.get(Item, item_id)
39	    if item is None or item.tenant_id != tenant_id:
40	        raise NotFoundError(message="Item not found", code="inventory.item_not_found")
41	    return item
42	
43	
44	async def create_item(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ItemCreate
46	) -> Item:
47	    """Create an item. Validates the category + base UoM exist, defaults costing_method from the
48	    category when omitted (D-020), and enforces tracking-only-on-stocked. Duplicate item_code →
49	    ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop)."""
50	    existing = (
51	        await session.execute(
52	            select(Item.id).where(
53	                Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.item_code == payload.item_code
54	            )
55	        )
56	    ).first()
57	    if existing is not None:
58	        raise ConflictError(
59	            message=f"An item with code {payload.item_code} already exists",
60	            code="inventory.item_code_conflict",
61	            details={"item_code": payload.item_code},
62	        )
63	    category = await get_category(session, tenant_id, payload.category_id)
64	    await get_uom(session, tenant_id, payload.base_uom_id)
65	
66	    item_type = ItemType(payload.item_type)
67	    tracking_mode = TrackingMode(payload.tracking_mode)
68	    _resolve_tracking(item_type, tracking_mode)
69	    costing_method = (
70	        CostingMethod(payload.costing_method)
71	        if payload.costing_method is not None
72	        else CostingMethod(category.default_costing_method)
73	    )
74	    item = Item(
75	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
76	        item_code=payload.item_code,
77	        name=payload.name,
78	        description=payload.description,
79	        item_type=item_type.value,
80	        category_id=payload.category_id,
81	        base_uom_id=payload.base_uom_id,
82	        costing_method=costing_method.value,
83	        tracking_mode=tracking_mode.value,
84	        is_active=payload.is_active,
85	        reorder_point=payload.reorder_point,
86	        reorder_quantity=payload.reorder_quantity,
87	    )
88	    session.add(item)
89	    await session.flush()
90	    return item
91	
92	
93	async def update_item(
94	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ItemUpdate
95	) -> Item:
96	    """Partial update of an item (D-010: mutate the loaded object). item_code and item_type are
97	    immutable and absent from the schema; a changed category/base UoM is re-validated and a changed
98	    tracking_mode is re-checked against the (immutable) item_type."""
99	    item = await get_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
100	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
101	    if data.get("category_id") is not None:
102	        await get_category(session, tenant_id, data["category_id"])
103	    if data.get("base_uom_id") is not None:
104	        await get_uom(session, tenant_id, data["base_uom_id"])
105	    if data.get("tracking_mode") is not None:
106	        _resolve_tracking(ItemType(item.item_type), TrackingMode(data["tracking_mode"]))
107	        data["tracking_mode"] = TrackingMode(data["tracking_mode"]).value
108	    if data.get("costing_method") is not None:
109	        data["costing_method"] = CostingMethod(data["costing_method"]).value
110	    for field, value in data.items():
111	        setattr(item, field, value)
112	    await session.flush()
113	    return item
114	
115	
116	async def list_items(
117	    session: AsyncSession,
118	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
119	    *,
120	    filters: ItemFilter,
121	    cursor: str | None,
122	    limit: int,
123	) -> Page[Item]:
124	    """Keyset-paginated item list ordered by item_code (D-014). Filters (type/category/active)
125	    narrow the set and fold into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot bleed across views."""
126	    stmt = select(Item).where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id)
127	    if filters.item_type is not None:
128	        stmt = stmt.where(Item.item_type == ItemType(filters.item_type).value)

39	def _client_ip(scope: Scope, trust_proxy: bool) -> str | None:
40	    """Audited client IP (D-010). Default: the raw transport peer (scope['client']). Only
41	    when ATLAS_TRUST_PROXY is on do we honor the LEFT-MOST X-Forwarded-For hop — otherwise a
42	    client could spoof its own audited IP just by sending the header."""
43	    if trust_proxy:

46	                first_hop = raw_value.decode("latin-1").split(",")[0].strip()

53	class RequestIdMiddleware:
54	    """Pure-ASGI: one uuid4-hex request id per request, exposed via ContextVar,
55	    request.state and the X-Request-ID response header.
56	
57	    It ALSO owns the D-007 tenancy-ContextVar reset, the D-009 current_permissions reset,
58	    and the D-010 audit-context (request_id, request_ip, actor_user_id) lifecycle:
59	    get_current_user sets the tenant/permissions/actor vars directly (no context manager),
60	    so this middleware captures reset tokens in a finally block — otherwise request A's
61	    context would leak into request B reusing the same worker/task. request_id and
62	    request_ip are seeded here at the edge; actor_user_id starts None (system/unauth) and is
63	    filled by get_current_user once the principal is known. All are reset on the way out, so
64	    the worker always restarts at the defaults."""
65	
66	    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, trust_proxy: bool) -> None:
67	        self.app = app
68	        self.trust_proxy = trust_proxy
69	
70	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
71	        if scope["type"] != "http":
72	            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
73	            return
74	        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
75	        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
76	        token = request_id_var.set(request_id)
77	        ip_token = request_ip_ctx.set(_client_ip(scope, self.trust_proxy))
78	        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(None)
79	        tenant_token = current_tenant_id.set(None)
80	        permissions_token = current_permissions.set(frozenset())
81	
82	        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
83	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
84	                MutableHeaders(scope=message)["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
85	            await send(message)
86	
87	        try:
88	            await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
89	        finally:
90	            current_permissions.reset(permissions_token)
91	            current_tenant_id.reset(tenant_token)
92	            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
93	            request_ip_ctx.reset(ip_token)
94	            request_id_var.reset(token)

126	    # D-013 replay short-circuit: a completed key with a matching body hash never runs the

"""Procurement constants (STRUCTURE §3): the vendor-master enums and the permission keys,
registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).

Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
cap, the finance precedent); PLAN 6.1 sits well under that.

**Payment-terms modeling (decided here).** A vendor carries ``payment_terms_days`` — a plain
integer net-days value (30 = NET30) — NOT a separate terms master/value-set. This matches how AP
already computes a bill's due date (bill_date + net days) and keeps v1 simple; richer term
schedules (e.g. 2/10 NET30 early-payment discounts, multi-instalment plans) are deferred per the
parity doc and would arrive as a terms entity referenced from the vendor. The field is stored with
a CHECK >= 0 on the vendor.

**Vendor codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant** (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_code)`` on
proc_vendors) — mirroring inventory ``item_code`` and the finance account ``code``: a vendor MASTER
carries no gapless document number (a code, not a number). The P2P DOCUMENTS in 6.2+ (requisitions,
POs, GRs) DO claim gapless numbers — a posted document in the D-012 sense — but the master does not.
"""

from enum import StrEnum

from app.core.rbac import register_permissions


class VendorStatus(StrEnum):
    """A vendor's lifecycle / usability state (parity: vendor master block levels).

    - ACTIVE: usable — new purchase orders may name this vendor (the only state 6.2+ accepts).
    - BLOCKED: temporarily barred — kept for history and existing open documents, but the P2P
      chain (6.2) refuses to raise a NEW PO against it (a soft block; the vendor can be unblocked
      back to ACTIVE).
    - INACTIVE: retired — no new business, retained for reporting and existing AP history.

    Transitions are unrestricted between the three (ACTIVE↔BLOCKED↔INACTIVE all allowed): a block
    is reversible and a retired vendor can be reactivated. The only rule the service enforces is
    that the target is a valid VendorStatus; no terminal state, because vendor history must stay
    referenceable and a mistaken retire/block must be undoable (the append-only ledger lives in
    finance AP, not here)."""

    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"


# The default net-days a vendor is created with when the payload omits it (NET30 — the common
# commercial default; AP's due-date math is bill_date + this many days). Stored on the vendor.
DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30


# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
# Two keys: read the vendor master (+ its approved items) vs create/edit it. Approved-item
# management is a vendor-master edit, so it rides VENDOR_MANAGE rather than a third key — adding an
# approved item is configuring the vendor, not a distinct privileged action (the inventory
# item/uom-conversion precedent: nested config shares the parent's manage key).
PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ = "procurement.vendor.read"
PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE = "procurement.vendor.manage"

register_permissions(
    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ,
    PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE,
    descriptions={
        PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_READ: "Read vendors and their approved items",
        PROCUREMENT_VENDOR_MANAGE: "Create and edit vendors and their approved items",
    },
)
